title: Could procrastination be beneficial
paragraphs: Procrastination is often seen as the enemy of productivity. Images of lazy people with feet up on desks or wasting time to dodge work spring to mind at the very mention of the word. And there are many things which indicate that procrastination is a problem which needs addressing. But could there be some benefits to it too?

We live in a high-octane world – always on the go, racing from one task to another. And at times, duties, be it work or personal, can feel relentless – with our nose constantly to the grindstone. Sometimes we just need to switch off, chill out and reboot. A little procrastination can help detach us from the pressures of modern life. According to psychotherapist F Diane Barth, watching TV, taking a long bath or listening to music can help us to ease off.

And it’s possible that procrastination has become more prevalent during the pandemic. With many countries going through lockdowns, some of us have suddenly found ourselves with more time – not having the hours of commutes, or options of social activities we once took for granted. Being at home, many of us quickly discovered that it is impossible to be productive 24-7. That extra relaxation can help us to be more productive or creative in the long run, allowing us to clear our minds and focus better.

The issue is that many of us see that time not working as lost time. And we almost develop a sense of guilt related to not making the most of every moment. German sociologist and economist Max Weber says that we’ve almost got to the point of believing that the busier we are, the better, and that there is a sense of morality connected with time usage. It seems important to remember that taking a little time away from yourself is not just slacking off.

So, while being productive is important, it seems that some amount of downtime and procrastination can help us to relax and become more focussed. The next time you feel really stressed, why not try wasting a little time? You might just like it.

vocabulary.entry: procrastination /prəˌkræstɪˈneɪʃn/ n. 拖延症；拖延行为
vocabulary.example: Procrastination often leads to unnecessary stress and missed deadlines.
vocabulary.translation: 拖延症常常会导致不必要的压力和错过截止日期。

vocabulary.entry: productivity /ˌprɒdʌkˈtɪvəti/ n. 生产力；工作效率
vocabulary.example: The new software has greatly improved office productivity.
vocabulary.translation: 这款新软件大幅提升了办公室的工作效率。

vocabulary.entry: dodge /dɒdʒ/ v. 逃避；躲避
vocabulary.example: He tried to dodge his responsibilities by leaving early.
vocabulary.translation: 他试图早早离开来逃避自己的责任。

vocabulary.entry: spring to mind /sprɪŋ tu maɪnd/ 立刻浮现于脑海
vocabulary.example: When I think of summer, the smell of sunscreen springs to mind.
vocabulary.translation: 一想到夏天，防晒霜的味道就立刻浮现在脑海里。

vocabulary.entry: address /əˈdres/ v. 解决；处理
vocabulary.example: The government needs to address the issue of housing shortages.
vocabulary.translation: 政府需要解决住房短缺的问题。

vocabulary.entry: high-octane /ˌhaɪ ˈɒkteɪn/ adj. 快节奏的；充满活力的
vocabulary.example: She loves the high-octane lifestyle of working in the city centre.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢在市中心工作的快节奏生活。

vocabulary.entry: on the go /ɒn ðə ɡəʊ/ 忙个不停；四处奔走
vocabulary.example: She's always on the go, juggling work and family commitments.
vocabulary.translation: 她总是忙个不停，要兼顾工作和家庭责任。

vocabulary.entry: relentless /rɪˈlentləs/ adj. 不间断的；永无止境的
vocabulary.example: The relentless rain ruined our plans for a picnic.
vocabulary.translation: 连绵不断的雨毁掉了我们的野餐计划。

vocabulary.entry: nose to the grindstone /nəʊz tu ðə ˈɡraɪndstəʊn/ 埋头苦干；辛勤劳作
vocabulary.example: He's had his nose to the grindstone for months to finish the project.
vocabulary.translation: 为了完成这个项目，他已经埋头苦干了好几个月。

vocabulary.entry: chill out /tʃɪl aʊt/ 放松；冷静下来
vocabulary.example: Let's just chill out at home tonight instead of going out.
vocabulary.translation: 今晚我们别出去了，就在家放松一下吧。

vocabulary.entry: reboot /ˌriːˈbuːt/ v. 重新启动；调整状态
vocabulary.example: After a short break, she felt rebooted and ready to continue working.
vocabulary.translation: 短暂休息后，她调整好了状态，准备继续工作。

vocabulary.entry: detach /dɪˈtætʃ/ v. 使脱离；使摆脱
vocabulary.example: It's important to detach yourself from work stress at the end of the day.
vocabulary.translation: 一天工作结束后，把自己从工作压力中解脱出来很重要。

vocabulary.entry: psychotherapist /ˌsaɪkəʊˈθerəpɪst/ n. 心理治疗师
vocabulary.example: The psychotherapist helped her deal with her anxiety issues.
vocabulary.translation: 这位心理治疗师帮她解决了焦虑问题。

vocabulary.entry: ease off /iːz ɒf/ 放松；缓和
vocabulary.example: The tension in the room eased off after he made a joke.
vocabulary.translation: 他开了个玩笑后，房间里的紧张气氛缓和了下来。

vocabulary.entry: prevalent /ˈprevələnt/ adj. 普遍的；盛行的
vocabulary.example: Flu is more prevalent during the winter months.
vocabulary.translation: 流感在冬季月份更为盛行。

vocabulary.entry: take for granted /teɪk fɔː ˈɡrɑːntɪd/ 认为……是理所当然的
vocabulary.example: We often take for granted the simple pleasures in life.
vocabulary.translation: 我们常常把生活中简单的快乐视为理所当然。

vocabulary.entry: 24-7 /ˌtwenti ˈfɔː ˈsevən/ 一天24小时、一周7天（全天候）
vocabulary.example: The convenience store is open 24-7 for customers' needs.
vocabulary.translation: 这家便利店全天候营业，满足顾客需求。

vocabulary.entry: in the long run /ɪn ðə lɒŋ rʌn/ 从长远来看
vocabulary.example: Eating a balanced diet is beneficial in the long run.
vocabulary.translation: 从长远来看，均衡饮食十分有益。

vocabulary.entry: guilt /ɡɪlt/ n. 愧疚感；内疚
vocabulary.example: She felt a sense of guilt for forgetting her friend's birthday.
vocabulary.translation: 她因为忘记了朋友的生日而感到愧疚。

vocabulary.entry: make the most of /meɪk ðə məʊst ɒv/ 充分利用
vocabulary.example: We should make the most of the sunny weather and go for a walk.
vocabulary.translation: 我们应该充分利用这晴朗的天气去散散步。

vocabulary.entry: morality /məˈræləti/ n. 道德；道德准则
vocabulary.example: The film raises questions about morality and justice.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影引发了人们对道德和正义的思考。

vocabulary.entry: slack off /slæk ɒf/ 偷懒；懈怠
vocabulary.example: Don't slack off during the exam period; keep studying hard.
vocabulary.translation: 考试期间别偷懒，要继续努力学习。

vocabulary.entry: downtime /ˈdaʊntaɪm/ n. 休息时间；停工时间
vocabulary.example: The company uses downtime to maintain its machines.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司利用停机时间维修机器。

vocabulary.entry: stress /stres/ n. 压力；紧张
vocabulary.example: Too much work stress can affect your physical health.
vocabulary.translation: 过多的工作压力会影响你的身体健康。

vocabulary.entry: focused /ˈfəʊkəst/ adj. 注意力集中的；专注的
vocabulary.example: She needs a quiet room to stay focused on her studies.
vocabulary.translation: 她需要一个安静的房间来专注于学习。

sentences.english: Procrastination is often seen as the enemy of productivity.
sentences.chinese: 拖延症常被视为生产力的大敌。

sentences.english: Images of lazy people with feet up on desks or wasting time to dodge work spring to mind at the very mention of the word.
sentences.chinese: 一提到这个词，人们脑海里就会浮现出懒人把脚翘在桌上、或是为逃避工作而消磨时间的画面。

sentences.english: And there are many things which indicate that procrastination is a problem which needs addressing.
sentences.chinese: 而且有诸多现象表明，拖延症是一个亟待解决的问题。

sentences.english: But could there be some benefits to it too?
sentences.chinese: 但它难道就没有任何益处吗？

sentences.english: We live in a high-octane world – always on the go, racing from one task to another.
sentences.chinese: 我们生活在一个快节奏的世界里，总是行色匆匆，忙完一项任务紧跟着就开始下一项任务。

sentences.english: And at times, duties, be it work or personal, can feel relentless – with our nose constantly to the grindstone.
sentences.chinese: 有时候，无论是工作还是私人事务，这些职责都显得永无止境，让我们不得不埋头苦干。

sentences.english: Sometimes we just need to switch off, chill out and reboot.
sentences.chinese: 有时候，我们就是需要彻底放松、舒缓身心、重新调整状态。

sentences.english: A little procrastination can help detach us from the pressures of modern life.
sentences.chinese: 适度的拖延，能帮我们暂时摆脱现代生活的压力。

sentences.english: According to psychotherapist F Diane Barth, watching TV, taking a long bath or listening to music can help us to ease off.
sentences.chinese: 心理治疗师F·黛安·巴特表示，看电视、泡个热水澡或是听听音乐，都能帮助我们放松下来。

sentences.english: And it’s possible that procrastination has become more prevalent during the pandemic.
sentences.chinese: 在疫情期间，拖延症的现象可能变得更为普遍。

sentences.english: With many countries going through lockdowns, some of us have suddenly found ourselves with more time – not having the hours of commutes, or options of social activities we once took for granted.
sentences.chinese: 随着许多国家实施封锁政策，我们中的一些人突然拥有了更多空闲时间——那些曾经习以为常的通勤时间没了，各类社交活动的选择也消失了。

sentences.english: Being at home, many of us quickly discovered that it is impossible to be productive 24-7.
sentences.chinese: 居家生活让很多人很快意识到，想要一天24小时、一周7天时刻保持高效是不可能的。

sentences.english: That extra relaxation can help us to be more productive or creative in the long run, allowing us to clear our minds and focus better.
sentences.chinese: 从长远来看，这些额外的放松时间能让我们更具效率和创造力，帮助我们理清思绪、更好地集中注意力。

sentences.english: The issue is that many of us see that time not working as lost time.
sentences.chinese: 问题在于，我们很多人都把不工作的时间看作是虚度光阴。

sentences.english: And we almost develop a sense of guilt related to not making the most of every moment.
sentences.chinese: 而且我们还会因为没能充分利用每一刻而产生愧疚感。

sentences.english: German sociologist and economist Max Weber says that we’ve almost got to the point of believing that the busier we are, the better, and that there is a sense of morality connected with time usage.
sentences.chinese: 德国社会学家兼经济学家马克斯·韦伯表示，我们几乎已经陷入了一种认知误区，认为越忙碌越好，并且将时间的利用方式和道德感挂钩。

sentences.english: It seems important to remember that taking a little time away from yourself is not just slacking off.
sentences.chinese: 但我们必须记住，给自己留一点放松的时间，绝不仅仅是偷懒。

sentences.english: So, while being productive is important, it seems that some amount of downtime and procrastination can help us to relax and become more focussed.
sentences.chinese: 因此，尽管保持高效很重要，但适度的休息和拖延，似乎能帮助我们放松身心、提升专注力。

sentences.english: The next time you feel really stressed, why not try wasting a little time? You might just like it.
sentences.chinese: 下次当你感到压力山大时，不妨试着“浪费”一点时间，说不定你会喜欢这种感觉。
